cases.prompt: I'm adding a new billing area to my React app. Where should the files go and how should I structure it?
expectations: Creates a single vertical slice at modules/billing/ with subfolders for pages, components, hooks, stores, services, utils, constants, and types.
Adds a curated public barrel at modules/billing/index.ts as the only cross-module entry point.
Adds a modules/billing/README.md describing what the module owns, its routes, and its data dependencies.
Does not create a utils module or a components module; technical building blocks belong in shared/.

cases.prompt: I've got this LineItemRow component that's only used by the invoice page. Should it go in shared/components?
expectations: Places the component in the narrowest scope that uses it, i.e. pages/{page}/components/ for a single page, not shared/components.
Explains the promotion ladder: one page -> page components, 2+ pages in a module -> modules/{feature}/components/, 2+ modules -> shared/components/, 2+ apps -> published design-system package.
States that a component is promoted only when a second consumer appears, never pre-placed.
Notes cross-module consumers must import through the module barrel (@/modules/{feature}), not a deep path.

cases.prompt: In my Zustand store I'm copying the fetched invoice list in so the UI can read it quickly. Is that okay?
expectations: Rejects mirroring server responses into the client store; the query/cache layer is the single source of truth for server data.
Explains the split: server state (fetched entities/lists/aggregates) lives in a query/cache layer; UI/client state (open dialogs, filters, wizard step) lives in a store.
Notes components must not fetch directly — they read server data from a data hook and UI state from a store selector.
Recommends one store unit per module accessed via the barrel, with selectors and a reset.

cases.prompt: Can you review this import for my module structure: import { InvoiceListPage } from "@/modules/invoice/pages/invoice-list/invoice-list";
expectations: Flags the deep internal path as a forbidden cross-module import that bypasses the barrel.
Corrects it to import from the barrel: import { InvoiceListPage } from "@/modules/invoice";
States that modules/{feature}/index.ts is the only thing other modules and the routing layer may import from.
May recommend running the conventions checklist, whose highest-value catches are state-origin leaks and deep cross-module imports.

cases.prompt: I want to add a settings screen with its own hook and a small sub-component. Should I just make one settings.tsx file?
expectations: Makes the page a directory, not a loose file, even when it starts as a single component.
Includes {page}.tsx, {page}.styles.ts, index.ts, and README.md, plus components/ and hooks/ for page-only code.
States pages/screens are always directories so growth has an obvious home and diffs stay readable.
Names the page directory in kebab-case with the component file matching (pages/{page}/{page}.tsx).

cases.prompt: I'll just drop a style={{ padding: 16 }} on this component to save time. Fine, right?
expectations: Rejects inline style literals in the component body on any stack.
Directs styling into a co-located {name}.styles.ts file (or {name}.module.css / styled-components, depending on the stack).
Explains that co-locating styling gives one place to audit spacing, theme correctness, and responsive behavior.
For Tailwind, exports named class strings composed with cn() (clsx + tailwind-merge), referenced as styles.header in JSX.
